_README: Planning scheme rules for the Meliora Subdivision Layout Generator.
Put this file NEXT TO the .html on meliorace.com. The tool fetches it on
load; if it is missing or unreadable the tool falls back to the copy built
into the page and says so in the progress log.
Editing this file is the whole job of keeping the tool current - there is
no need to re-issue the HTML. Adding a rule set here also adds it to the
Planning scheme dropdown.
A council can appear more than once where the scheme sets different lot
types or precincts (BCC standard vs small lot, ICC established vs new
suburban). Only ONE entry per council carries `lga_match` - that is the one
auto-detect picks. The others are chosen by hand from the dropdown.
After checking an entry against the published code, set its `verified`
date. That date is printed on the PSP Rules Summary.
Fields: min_lot / min_rear_lot are NET areas in m2 (the access handle is
excluded from a rear lot in all four schemes). min_frontage in m.
min_access_1 / min_access_2plus are TENURE widths in m. driveway_min is the
constructed pavement width, null where the code is silent. max_access_len
in m, null where the code sets none. min_rect is [width, depth] in m that
must fit inside the lot, null where the code sets none; min_rect_setback is
how far back from the frontage that rectangle must sit.

`access_table` is the real rule in every scheme - the width steps with the number of lots served, and in Brisbane also with the length of the access way. min_access_1 / min_access_2plus are only a fallback for a rule set with no table.
REVIEW DATE: quarterly. See claude/psp-rules-report.md in the project.
This file is GENERATED by mce-planning-rules (scripts/build_rules.py) from 23/10/2026 – edit the skill's rules, not this file.
Extra fields (tools that don't know them ignore them): max_rear_lots_per_frontage_lot (MBRC: 1), tenure_options (MBRC adds common property).

codes: Subdivision code, Section 9.4.10

The code that applies to reconfiguring a lot in Brisbane. Note the name - Brisbane calls it the Subdivision code, not a Reconfiguring a lot code, and it sits at 9.4.10 in Part 9 (Other development codes).
Table 9.4.10.3.B Part 1 — Standard lots

Minimum lot size, minimum rectangle dimension, and average lot width & minimum frontage for a standard lot in the Low density residential, Character residential, Low-medium density residential and Emerging community zones.
Table 9.4.10.3.B Part 3 — Rear lots
The same three dimensions for a rear lot. Note (3) to the table confirms the minimum lot size is calculated excluding the access way.
Standard drawings BSD-2021 and BSD-2022
Vehicle crossing / driveway for a single dwelling, and for a rear allotment access - crossover width, wing flares and the truncation where the access strip meets the frontage.
Transport, access, parking and servicing planning scheme policy SC6.31, section 4.12.1, Table 11

Where the rear lot access way width actually lives - the Subdivision code refers out to it. Table 11 is keyed on the number of DWELLING UNITS served and on whether the access way is more or less than 40m from the dedicated road, and it sets the concrete driveway spec as well as the easement width.
rules: Table 9.4.10.3.B Part 1: a standard residential lot in the Low density residential zone is 450m², with a minimum rectangle of 14m x 20m and an average lot width and minimum frontage of 15m. If the site suits the SMALL LOT provisions, switch the planning scheme to the BCC small lot rule set rather than overriding the minimum by hand - the frontage and rectangle change with it.

Table 9.4.10.3.B Part 3, note (3). Brisbane requires a rear lot to be materially larger than a standard lot and the access way does not count towards it. This is what rules out most battle-axe layouts on a small parent lot. The rear lot must also hold a 14m x 20m rectangle and average 15m wide.

Table 9.4.10.3.B Part 1. The column is 'Average lot width and minimum frontage', so 15m is both the frontage AND the average width - a lot that pinches behind a wide frontage does not comply. 10m is the SMALL LOT figure, not the standard one.
Table 9.4.10.3.B Parts 1 and 3. A rectangle of these dimensions has to fit inside the lot. An area-compliant lot that is long and thin fails here, which is why the tool tests it as well as the area.
1-3 dwellings within 40m of the road: 3.5m easement, 2.5m driveway. 4-5: 4.0m / 3.1m. 6 or more: 6.5m / 5.5m. Over 40m from the road, 1-5 dwellings: 6.0m easement, 3.1m driveway plus passing lanes

Transport, access, parking and servicing planning scheme policy SC6.31 Table 11. Note how much narrower this is than the 4m/6m most people assume - a single rear lot within 40m of the road needs only a 3.5m easement, which on a small parent lot is the difference between a compliant rear lot and a non-compliant one. The width steps up with the number of DWELLINGS, not lots, and again past 40m. The easement must be at least 3.5m wide anyway where services run alongside the driveway, and includes a single chord truncation at the property alignment. A driveway trafficked by refuse vehicles is never less than 6.5m.

Note (1) to Table 9.4.10.3.B: the minimum lot size is calculated INCLUDING the land area of a truncation to be dedicated as road, provided the minimum rectangle still fits in the balance. The tool sizes lots without relying on that, which is conservative.
single chord truncation at the property alignment

SC6.31 section 4.12.1(5)(a). Confirms the truncation the tool draws where the access strip meets the frontage. The vehicle crossing from the back of kerb to the property alignment follows BSD-2021, BSD-2024 and BSD-2025.
1 in 10 short axis, 1 in 15 long axis
Subdivision code AO2.2. Average slope across the lot. Only bites on lots under 450m2 - a standard 450m2+ lot has no slope limit under this AO.
Subdivision code AO2.3. The minimum rectangle has to sit on existing slope flatter than 1 in 5, BEFORE earthworks - so a lot that only works after a big cut does not comply.

ICC.label: Ipswich City Plan — Established suburban lot
ICC.council: Ipswich City Plan, Reconfiguring a Lot Code 9.4.1 (Established suburban lot)
ICC.zone: Low density residential zone — Established suburban lot
ICC.verified_note: Read from Tables 9.4.1.3.5 and 9.4.1.3.10 and PO3.1-PO3.5 of the Reconfiguring a Lot Code. The document is footed 'Ipswich City Plan 2025', not 'Ipswich Plan 2024'. It carries no printed effective date. The minimum lot size can be overridden by the Building Height and Density Overlay OV6, whose figures are NOT in this code and are not applied by the tool.
codes: Reconfiguring a Lot Code, Section 9.4.1

Lot size, frontage, hatchet lots and access for a reconfiguration. Ipswich does not set one minimum for the zone - the minimum follows the LOT TYPE (large, established suburban, new suburban, built to boundary), and an infill splitter in an established suburb is an Established suburban lot.
Table 9.4.1.3.5 — Established Suburban Lot Size, Frontage and Special Characteristics
The row that governs a normal Ipswich infill splitter: lot size, frontage, and the building rectangle.
Table 9.4.1.3.10 — Hatchet Lot Access Handles and Access Easements
Tenure width, combined width and constructed driveway width for a hatchet lot access handle, by lot type.
Building Height and Density Overlay OV6
Can substitute a different minimum lot size or density. The code says so but does not state the figures. This tool applies 450m² - CHECK THE OVERLAY before relying on a pass.
rules: between 450m² and 2,000m², or as stated in Overlay OV6

Table 9.4.1.3.5. 450m² is the FLOOR for an Established suburban lot, not the rule - the Building Height and Density Overlay can require more on a given site, and its figures are not in this code. Ipswich also expects a depth ratio of about 1:2 (frontage to depth).

There is NO separate minimum area for a hatchet lot in this code - it takes the minimum of its own lot type. The note under Table 9.4.1.3.10 confirms 'the area of the access handle is excluded from the area of the lot'.
Table 9.4.1.3.5. Frontage does not vary with slope in this code; slope instead governs which lot types are available and triggers the Difficult Topography and Landslide Overlay Code above 15%.
10m x 15m, clear of the first 6m from the frontage

Table 9.4.1.3.5: the lot must contain a rectangle suitable for building purposes of 10m x 15m (or 9m x 15m where a boundary wall is nominated along one side boundary) 'in that part of the lot which is not within 6m of the frontage'. The 6m exclusion is unusual and is easy to miss - the tool applies it.
Front lot of a hatchet subdivision
minimum width 15m and a 9m x 15m building area
PO3.2. The front lot has to work in its own right. Access handles or easements are located on only ONE side of the front lot.
4.0m to one lot; 4.0m plus 1.0m where two hatchet lots share it; 3.0m constructed driveway in both cases

Table 9.4.1.3.10, Large lot or Established suburban lot row. Note this is narrower than the 6.0m several other south-east Queensland councils require for two or more lots. The table has no row for a New suburban or Built to boundary hatchet lot. Where the strip is shared, reciprocal easement rights are required, and the handle needs a constructed driveway plus underground electricity and telecommunications for its full length.
AO3.5. Beyond 50m, or where the easement serves more than one hatchet lot, a passing bay is required at intervals no greater than 50m from each end.
one behind any full frontage lot
PO3.1(e), and PO3.1(f) requires that a hatchet lot adjoins no more than five other premises.

combined access strip - minimum plus 1m, reciprocal easement rights required

LCC.verified_note: Read from Tables 9.4.6.3.2, 9.4.6.3.4 and 9.4.6.3.5 of the Reconfiguring a lot code, effective 01/07/2025. Every figure previously carried for Logan was wrong, including an average lot size rule that does not exist. Check Table 9.4.6.3.3 for a LOCAL PLAN override before relying on these - the Loganholme local plan, for example, imposes a 3:1 depth to width ratio.
codes: Reconfiguring a lot code, Section 9.4.6
Lot size, frontage, rear lots and access for a reconfiguration in Logan. The zone and precinct are the Low density residential zone, Suburban precinct.
Table 9.4.6.3.2 — Reconfiguring a lot
Minimum lot size, minimum frontage (normal, cul-de-sac and corner) and maximum depth to width ratio by zone and precinct.
Table 9.4.6.3.4 — Additional requirements for rear lots
Minimum area clear of the access strip, maximum access strip length, and the access strip width and pavement width by the number of dwellings served.
Table 9.4.6.3.3 — Reconfiguring a lot: local plans
An ALTERNATIVE to Table 9.4.6.3.2 where a local plan applies. AO3 makes the two tables alternatives, so a local plan can change the numbers below. Check it for every Logan site.
rules: Table 9.4.6.3.2, Low density residential zone - Suburban precinct. Not 350m².

Table 9.4.6.3.4, column 2 'Minimum area clear of access strip'. A Logan rear lot is 100m² bigger than a standard lot and the access strip does not count - this is the criterion most likely to kill a Logan battle-axe.
12.5m normal, 10m to a cul-de-sac, 15m on a corner lot
Table 9.4.6.3.2. The tool applies 12.5m. A corner lot frontage is measured from the back of the truncation along the nominated frontage.
Table 9.4.6.3.2, Low density residential zone - Suburban precinct, 'Minimum frontage (cul-de-sac)'. A lot on a cul-de-sac head needs only 10m, not the 12.5m a standard lot needs.

Table 9.4.6.3.2, same row set, 'Minimum frontage (corner lot)'. A Logan corner lot needs MORE frontage than a standard lot, not less - 15m against 12.5m. Applied to any lot this tool measures frontage to two different streets on.

There is NO average lot size rule in the Logan Reconfiguring a lot code. The tool previously applied a 500m² average, which does not exist and would have failed compliant layouts. The only across-the-reconfiguration rule is a frontage diversity standard in Table 9.4.6.3.5, and it is only triggered when creating 10 or more lots - so it never applies to a splitter.
1 dwelling: 4.0m reserve, 3.0m pavement. 2 to 4 dwellings: 5.5m reserve, 3.0m pavement, passing bays required. 5 or more: 8.0m reserve, 5.5m pavement

Table 9.4.6.3.4. On-site refuse collection is required from four dwellings up. A passing bay is 2.5m wide (5.5m total driveway width) by 6m long with 45 degree tapers, one for every 30m where the driveway exceeds 30m.
Table 9.4.6.3.4. Shorter than most - Village precinct gets 50m and Large suburban 60m. A deep Logan lot can fail on handle length before it fails on anything else.
not applicable in the Suburban precinct

Table 9.4.6.3.2 gives 'NA' for this precinct. Ratios start at the Large suburban precinct (3:1). But the Loganholme local plan Suburban residential precinct in Table 9.4.6.3.3 does impose 3:1, so check the local plan.

Planning scheme policy – Integrated design / Waste
Driveway, crossover and bin-pad details Council asks for on small ROLs.
rules: Suburban neighbourhood (and Coastal communities) precinct example, max density 11 lots/ha. These are examples – an alternative must be argued against the performance outcomes. Next generation precinct has no minimum (10–25 lots/ha).

one rear lot only behind a full-frontage lot
PO5. A lot with no road frontage is 'not supported'; two or more rear lots on one handle draw an information request – use common property.
Council RFIs: 'access handles for rear lots are to be a minimum of 5 metres wide' (driveway, services and bin pickup). 4.0 m accepted twice; 3.25 m refused.
Council prefers common property to access easements for 3 or more lots; 6.0 m crossover for at least 10 m into the site, then 3 m with a 10 m passing bay.
Common property is a real third option in Moreton Bay and the one Council steers 3+ lot layouts towards.

not_checked: Water and sewer connection and any Urban Utilities requirements, including whether each new lot can be serviced and where the connection points fall.
Stormwater - lawful point of discharge, overland flow paths, inter-allotment drainage and any downstream easement that a rear lot needs.

Overlays: flood, waterway corridor, bushfire, landslide, biodiversity, significant vegetation, acid sulfate soils, heritage, transport noise corridor, airport operations, and any local or neighbourhood plan. In Ipswich this includes the Building Height and Density Overlay OV6, which can set the minimum lot size; in Logan a local plan can replace the whole lot size table.
Existing easements, covenants, building format plans and statutory encumbrances on the parent title.
Earthworks, retaining, batters and whether each lot has a usable building platform at a sensible level.
Whether an existing dwelling or structure that is to be retained still complies with the dwelling house code on its new, smaller lot - setbacks, site cover, private open space and parking.
Fire hydrant coverage. The design test is 90m to the furthest point of the lot (SEQ Water Supply and Sewerage Design and Construction Code cl 8.8.8), proved on a reach-out plan.
Passing bays, on-site refuse manoeuvring and the design vehicle for an access handle, all of which are triggered by the number of lots served.
Infrastructure charges, contributions and the cost of the works.
The boundaries themselves. Every dimension on these sheets comes from the DCDB and is preliminary until a cadastral survey is done.
